author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I am willing to let the data contracts stay manual for this specific release. The physical stock is already committed, so the risk of schema drift is manageable right now. However, I will only accept that if the acceptance criteria for the allocation logic are fully governed. We need a formal, strict sign off on the tests before the trucks leave the distribution centre. This ensures the audit trail is complete and the legal duty to have reasonable stock available is met. If we skip that governance step, I will not sign off on the deployment, regardless of the timeline pressure. I am trading the speed of automated contract validation for the security of a fully audited release.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are trading the speed of automated contract validation for the security of a fully audited release, indicating a conscious decision to give up one benefit to accept another.
